title: Summary
text: This agent run refactored the retrieval pipeline to support hybrid search: combining dense vector similarity with BM25 keyword scoring. The previous implementation used vector-only retrieval, which underperformed on exact-match queries. Decision: Replace single-stage vector retrieval with a two-stage pipeline: BM25 candidate retrieval → reranking by cosine similarity.

title: Changes Made
text: src/retrieval/indexer.py: Added BM25 index construction alongside existing vector index (+84/-12). src/retrieval/search.py: Replaced vector_search() with hybrid_search() (+61/-38). src/retrieval/reranker.py: New file — cosine reranker over BM25 candidates (+47/-0). tests/test_retrieval.py: Added 14 new test cases (+112/-5).

title: Affected Code Symbols
text: indexer.py::IndexBuilder.build() now builds both BM25 and vector indices. indexer.py::IndexBuilder.build_bm25() is a new method. search.py::vector_search() is deprecated, replaced by hybrid_search(). search.py::hybrid_search() is the new entry point. reranker.py::CosineReranker is a new class. reranker.py::CosineReranker.rerank() reranks a list of BM25 candidates.

title: Evidence & Benchmarks
text: Retrieval quality MRR@10 on dev set (250 queries): Vector only 0.61 MRR@10 / 0.74 Recall@20. BM25 only 0.54 MRR@10 / 0.68 Recall@20. Hybrid BM25 + rerank 0.71 MRR@10 / 0.82 Recall@20. Latency increased by ~18ms p95 due to BM25 candidate expansion, within the acceptable budget of <50ms.

title: Open Questions
text: Should BM25 candidate count (currently k=50) be configurable per query type? Is the current tokenizer (whitespace split) sufficient, or do we need a subword tokenizer for BM25? Should we persist the BM25 index to disk to avoid rebuild on startup?
